chapter: Life in New York in the 1940s
title: Why Edison avoided drugs; pot-only era before bebop
summary: Edison says he learned from others' mistakes and that before bop musicians used only pot, with rare exceptions.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You know, when you consider that atmosphere, you're playing in the smoke.
But Frank or the other ones didn't go for it, you know. The musicians, you know -- I've never -- I've
Well, you got your kicks from playing.
Oh, yeah. And I don't drink. I quit smoking cigarettes about 10 years ago. But I could never see going the way that somebody else is going, which is killing them. If it's killing them.
As soon as you could see --
Yeah, I've always wanted to benefit by other guys' mistakes. If it's hurting him and killing him; I want to live as long as I can so why would I want to kill myself like that.
You know, I think the idea of the heroin thing is a bit repulsive to me.
It is.

Right, you're no good to nobody, no good to yourself. After you do it, you have to sleep and you nod, you know. And it just creates crime because when they haven't got money for it they'll get it someplace, you know.
Well, that was really sad but fortunately that has sort of -- people have seen the light to a considerable extent.
Yeah. Well, that was an era that became popular around the bee-pop days, you know.
Yeah, the two went together in some sense.

Pot.

Yeah, to smoke, you know. And the big bands, that's as far as they went, you know. Very rarely you would hear of anyone in the days that we're talking about that were so fantastically New York, was going for anything else but pot. Every now and then you would hear of a guy going way out on a limb trying something else, like the trumpet player with Jimmy Luneford, Steve -- I forget his -- he was a high note guy. (Tommy Stevenson)
Yeah, I remember him.
He went off the deep end, you know, using horse and everything.
That was early.
Yeah, that was early. But that was before anybody even knew what it was, you know. And -- but it was a very rare, rare occasion, you know, that you would find musicians doing that.
